name: Standing Calf Raise
grip: Neutral grip holding dumbbells at sides with arms fully extended.
description: Raise heels off the ground by performing bilateral ankle plantar flexion with knees softly extended, emphasizing the gastrocnemius under loaded stretch.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms straight at your sides.
Step onto a raised calf block or sturdy platform with the balls of both feet on the edge and heels hanging freely.
Stand tall with chest lifted, core braced, and knees softly extended without locking them out.
instructions: Lower your heels smoothly below the level of the block into deep ankle dorsiflexion until you feel a complete stretch through your calves.
Press forcefully through the balls of both feet into full plantar flexion, elevating your heels as high as possible onto your tiptoes.
Hold the peak contraction briefly at the top, squeezing your calves firmly.
Lower your heels in a slow, controlled descent back into the deep bottom stretch before initiating the next repetition.
cues: Press through the balls of the feet.
Keep knees motionless and softly unlocked.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees to bounce or turn the movement into a squat.
Cutting the bottom range of motion short and failing to reach a full stretch.
Swinging dumbbells or using upper body momentum.

logging.example: Two 16 kg dumbbells: record 16 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Record the mass of an individual dumbbell rather than the combined total of the pair.

variantNote: Standing bilateral calf raise performed on a raised block holding dumbbells, keeping knees straight to recruit the gastrocnemius.
